metadata.description: Two-stage process: 1) Tuning parameter optimization (grid search, RMSE-minimizing) 2) Final benchmark run with N_COST_REPS averaged CPU timing

cost_measurement.note: Values represent mean CPU seconds over N_COST_REPS runs divided by signal length to give µs/sample. No JIT, no vectorization — conservative baseline for embedded DSP/FPGA deployment estimation.

scenario_description.parameters: Ramp +5 Hz/s starting at t=0.3s, ending t=1.0s
Instantaneous Phase Jump +60 deg at t=0.7s
scenario_description.dynamics: Phase Discontinuity (instantaneous phase jump → freq. spike)

scenario_description.motivation: Composite scenario motivated by EMT simulation studies of IBR islanding events. Parameters (RoCoF=-6 Hz/s, phase jumps 40°/80°, ring-down 3 Hz, harmonics 5th+7th) are representative of documented IBR transient signatures. Synthetic signal at fs=10 kHz.
scenario_description.parameters: 5 s: (0-1s) IBR steady w/ 5th & 7th harmonics; (1.0s) +40 deg phase jump; (1.2-2.5s) ROCOF -6 Hz/s (60→52.8 Hz); (2.5s) +80 deg phase jump; (2.5-3.5s) 2nd-order ring-down (f_osc=3 Hz, σ=3 s⁻¹); (3.5-5s) harmonic-rich steady-state w/ impulsive noise.
scenario_description.noise: Gaussian background sigma_g=0.003 pu + non-Gaussian impulsive spikes sigma_imp=0.05 pu (p=0.0005 per sample). Note: figure caption sigma=0.05 refers to impulsive spike amplitude.
scenario_description.dynamics: Composite: phase jumps, fast RoCoF, ring-down, non-Gaussian disturbances.

monte_carlo.description: Monte Carlo robustness analysis over 30 independent noise realisations for all 13 estimators with fixed optimised parameters. Reports mean ± std of RMSE [Hz], FE_max [Hz], RFE_max [Hz/s], and Trip-Risk Duration [s] per method and scenario.

cpu_authoritative.description: Definitive per-sample CPU cost [µs] for the Pareto reference scenario (IBR_MultiEvent). These values are authoritative for the submitted run. Paper Table V may show slightly different values if produced with a different N_COST_REPS or hardware configuration.
cpu_authoritative.timer: time.process_time() — single-threaded CPU time, no JIT
cpu_authoritative.note: Timed with N_COST_REPS=20. If paper Table V numbers are ~25% higher for Kalman-family methods (EKF/EKF2/UKF), this reflects a prior run with higher N_COST_REPS or a different CPU load condition. The json values are from the current hardware: Intel64 Family 6 Model 170 Stepping 4, GenuineIntel.

statistical_analysis._ieee_report_standard: Statistical analysis following IEEE Signal Processing Society reporting conventions. All tests: alpha=0.05, non-parametric, pre-registered H0 hypotheses. Effect sizes: rank-biserial r (Mann-Whitney U), eta^2 (Kruskal-Wallis), Spearman rho. Bonferroni correction applied family-wise over executed tests.

H1.description: H0: Trip-Risk duration is identically distributed across all estimators under Composite Islanding (Scenario D). Kruskal-Wallis, two-sided, α=0.05.

H2.description: H0: RA-EKF (EKF2) RMSE and EKF RMSE are equal in distribution under Composite Islanding (Scenario D). Mann-Whitney U, two-sided, α=0.05.

H3.description: H0: ρ=0 — no monotonic rank correlation between per-estimator RMSE on Ramp (Scenario B) and RMSE on Composite Islanding (Scenario D). Spearman, two-sided, α=0.05.

H4.description: H0: Window-based and model-based estimators have identical RMSE distributions under IBR Multi-Event (Scenario E). Mann-Whitney U, two-sided, α=0.05.

H5.description: H0: ρ=0 — Computational cost (CPU µs/sample) and Trip-Risk duration are statistically independent across estimators in IBR Multi-Event (Scenario E). Spearman, two-sided, α=0.05. Rejection would support the Pareto cost-safety trade-off claim.

H6.description: H0: RA-EKF Ramp RMSE ≥ SRF-PLL Ramp RMSE. Alternative (one-sided): RA-EKF has strictly lower Ramp RMSE. Mann-Whitney U, less, α=0.05.

H7.description: H0: RMSE variance is homogeneous across all estimators under Composite Islanding (Scenario D). Levene test, two-sided, α=0.05.

H8.description: H0: ρ=0 — Per-estimator RMSE rank under Magnitude Step (Scenario A) does not predict RMSE rank under IBR Multi-Event (Scenario E). Rejection supports the claim that standard tests are insufficient. Spearman, two-sided, α=0.05.

H9.description: H0: Koopman-RKDPmu and RA-EKF have identical Trip-Risk distributions under IBR Multi-Event (Scenario E). Mann-Whitney U, two-sided, α=0.05.

H10.description: H0: Per-estimator RMSE values under Composite Islanding (Scenario D) are normally distributed. Shapiro-Wilk per estimator, α=0.05. Non-normality validates the choice of non-parametric tests H1-H9.

cross_scenario_spearman.interpretation: Spearman ρ for each (scenario_i, scenario_j) pair computed over 8 estimators. Low ρ between a standard IEC/IEEE scenario and an IBR-specific scenario indicates that standard compliance does not predict IBR stress performance.

estimator_clusters.interpretation: K-means (k=3) partitions estimators by (Islanding RMSE, Multi-Event RMSE, log-CPU cost, Multi-Event Trip-Risk). Clusters correspond to: low-cost/high-risk, moderate-cost/moderate-risk, and high-cost/low-risk regimes.

cpu_trip_E.description: Pareto front: min(CPU µs/sample, Trip-Risk [s]) — Scenario E
cpu_trip_E.note: EKF2 (RA-EKF) is Pareto-dominated by EKF in Multi-Event (Scenario E): EKF CPU=16.9µs < EKF2 CPU=58.1µs, EKF Trip=296.5ms < EKF2 Trip=116.2ms. However, EKF2's advantage is scenario-specific to Islanding (Scenario D): EKF2 Trip=0.00ms vs EKF Trip=0ms — a 0× safety advantage under phase-step islanding.

cpu_rmse_D.description: Pareto front: min(CPU µs/sample, RMSE [Hz]) — Scenario D
cpu_rmse_D.note: In Scenario D (Islanding) RMSE-vs-CPU space, EKF2 and SOGI both achieve very low RMSE. SOGI achieves the lowest RMSE overall in this scenario (see results.IBR_Nightmare.notable_findings).

IBR_Nightmare.__interpretation: rank_std=0.0 for all methods indicates ranking is fully stable across all bootstrap resamples. RMSE differences between methods exceed within-method noise variance, confirming statistical robustness of the reported rankings.

IBR_MultiEvent.__interpretation: rank_std=0.0 for all methods indicates ranking is fully stable across all bootstrap resamples. RMSE differences between methods exceed within-method noise variance, confirming statistical robustness of the reported rankings.

bootstrap_rank_confidence.interpretation: Bootstrap rank CI (5th–95th percentile over 1000 replicates). Narrow CI → stable rank across noise realisations. Wide CI → rank is sensitive to noise conditions.
